tara-support: FYI customer NimblePay reporting a sudden surge of 429s on their dedicated pool after a product release. They say it coincides with long-context invoice generation workloads. Escalating. ticket: #C-4821
ryan-sre: Can you paste the error payloads? 429 from our side or upstream auth?
tara-support: Most are 429s with body: `rate_limit_exceeded: kv_cache_evictions` and spikes in latency ~2s for token generation. Sample log attached below.
amy-cs: Customer says it happens when they send ~12k token contexts repeatedly. They reproduced with a small script.
miguel-eng: sounds like KV cache pressure + fragmentation. Which dedicated slab config for their capacity?
tara-support: Dedicated pool d-cap-7, 4xA100, autoscale enabled with burst. Alloc slab: default.
ryan-sre: Pulling recent metrics... @kv-monitor-bot can you dump eviction rate, KV usage, and slab fragmentation for d-cap-7 tenant nimblepay-tn?
kv-monitor-bot: Eviction rate: 85/s -> 220/s over 12:36-12:42. KV occupancy 93%. Fragmentation ratio: 0.42. Longctx hit ratio drop: 68% -> 30%. Autoscale didn't trigger because free GPU memory < 5% threshold.
miguel-eng: That fragmentation number is high. Likely many large KV entries from longctx, causing heavy compaction and slow GC; eviction storms produce tail latency and token-level throttles.
sara.ops: Did autoscaler log any cooldown/backoff events?
ryan-sre: Autoscaler shows repeated scale attempts aborted due to quota check failing (burst capacity limit hit). So we had no scale out and evictions mounted.
amy-cs: Customer is concerned about billing spikes and 429s during peak. They want immediate mitigation and a long-term fix.
miguel-eng: Immediate mitigations: 1) apply tenant-specific KV quota increase for nimblepay-tn to allow more slab headroom (temp) 2) enable `kv_prevent_large_entries` prompt limiter or recommend chunking contexts >8k tokens 3) reduce eviction aggressiveness by adjusting `kvcache_eviction_ratio` from 0.8 -> 0.65 on pool (careful) 4) add fallback route to a smaller model variant for super-long requests.
tara-support: Can we do (1) and (4) quickly? Customer wants a patch within the hour.
ryan-sre: I can bump tenant KV quota by 20% and flip a routing rule to fallback to gptx-compact for requests >10k tokens. Doing now.
kv-monitor-bot: Action: tenant_kv_quota +20% applied at 12:58 UTC. Routing rule active at 13:02 UTC.
kv-monitor-bot: Post-change metrics: eviction rate dropped to 45/s, KV occupancy 82%, longctx hit ratio stabilized at 62%. 429s fell to near-zero within 3m.
amy-cs: NimblePay confirms 429s have stopped. They still want a timeline for durable fix.
miguel-eng: Long-term: (A) enable per-tenant slab segregation on d-cap pools to avoid noisy neighbor spillover, (B) implement adaptive slab compaction that prioritizes longctx-friendly allocations, (C) autoscaler change: allow emergency one-off burst ad-hoc for ticketed incidents or quick add-on capacity. I'll own design doc.
sara.ops: Please add runbook steps to product incident playbook: detection alert thresholds, quick bump command, rollback.
tara-support: I'll update the ticket and send customer post-mortem + recommended client changes (chunking + retry-backoff).
ryan-sre: Followups: miguel to PR design doc by EOD, sara to update runbook, I to propose autoscale policy change to infra by Monday.
amy-cs: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ryan-sre: Noting for postmortem: cause=kv-cache fragmentation + quota bottleneck + autoscale quota block -> eviction storm -> token-level throttles.
